title: Eval Quality Monitoring Demo - Montgomery Health

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Morales (Redwood Product), Jordan Kim (Redwood Solutions), Priya Shah (Montgomery Head of AI), Marcus Lee (CTO), Dana Gomez (Clinical Informatics), Rafael Ortiz (Security), Evan Brooks (Data Engineer)

Summary (auto): demo of Redwood Eval/Quality Monitoring, focus on prompt sets, regression detection, A/B comparisons. Questions about PHI, KMS, audit logs, and pilot cadence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood, this is Samir and Lina with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Priya Shah: Good, thanks. We are excited—Priya here. We've been struggling with drift on our clinical summarization models and want something to catch regressions earlier.
[00:15] Marcus Lee: Hi, Marcus. Our main ask is we need deterministic evals for reg reviews, and low false positives on alerts, otherwise clinicians get alert fatigue.
[00:28] Samir Patel: Totally, that's the kind of thing we built the Eval product for. Quick agenda: we'll show prompt-set based evals, setting baselines, alerting rules, then A/B comparisons and how rollouts tie into Console and API.
[00:40] Dana Gomez: Quick call out—these involve PHI, so we need to understand retention and KMS/HSM options.
[00:48] Jordan Kim: Noted. We'll cover encryption and audit logs in security section, and we can follow up with a security pack.
[01:02] Avery Chen: Kicking off the demo — Lina, can you share your screen?
[01:05] Lina Morales: Yep, sharing now... okay, you should see the Eval dashboard. At the top: prompt sets. We organize prompts by test suite: clinical-summaries-1000, discharge-500, etc., you can upload CSV or integrate via API.
[01:22] Evan Brooks: Is there a template for prompt columns? We have structured EMR fields we want to include in prompts.
[01:28] Lina Morales: Yes, we have a sample template—columns for prompt_id, input_text, expected_output, category, tags, and metadata. We'll share that after. The API supports streaming results back and also returns structured scoring metrics.
[01:44] Samir Patel: For the Montgomery pipeline, you'd likely want to include ROUGE, clinical-entity-presence checks, hallucination heuristics, and a custom exact-match for critical data points like med lists.
[01:56] Priya Shah: How flexible are the metrics? Can we plug in our own evaluation function?
[02:02] Samir Patel: Yes, you can bring custom metrics via a small lambda-style eval or run locally and post results; Console supports custom metric definitions and thresholding.
[02:15] Marcus Lee: About thresholds—we want to alert only when regressions cross both stat sig and clinical impact thresholds. Is that supported?
[02:24] Lina Morales: We support multi-condition alerts: absolute delta, percent change, and custom severity rules. You can require both: e.g., >= 5% drop and p < 0.05.
[02:36] Rafael Ortiz: Does alerting integrate with our ticketing—Jira and Slack?
[02:40] Jordan Kim: Yes, webhooks, Slack, email, and native Jira integration. Alerts include a sample diff view and link to failing prompts.
[02:50] Dana Gomez: Can we see an example?
[02:54] Lina Morales: Sure, switching to an example regression. Here's an A/B comparison we ran last week between model-v1 and model-v2. You can see the distribution plot, per-prompt diffs, and a ranked list of top failing prompts.
[03:10] (audio glitch)
[03:15] Priya Shah: Sorry, cut out for a sec — can you zoom into the per-prompt table?
[03:20] Lina Morales: Yep, table shows prompt_id, input snippet, v1_output, v2_output, metric scores, and tags. You can open any prompt to view tokens and token-level attention highlights — helpful to debug hallucinations.
[03:35] Marcus Lee: This is great — does the system support rolling A/B in production so we can route 10% to model-v2 and collect evals?
[03:44] Samir Patel: Yep, integration with routing policies. We can do canary rollouts by user cohort, route, or region. Requests get flagged and evals are run asynchronously, then effects show up in the dashboard.
[03:58] Evan Brooks: For the async evals, are outputs stored? We have retention requirements for PHI—we can't keep raw prompts longer than X days.
[04:07] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, need to know retention policy and ability to auto-delete and store only hashes.
[04:12] Avery Chen: We support configurable retention per-tenant, auto-delete policies, and option to store only hashed inputs. For Private/Dedicated, you can bring your own KMS; we also offer HSM-backed key management for enterprise.
[04:26] Rafael Ortiz: And audit logs for all eval runs?
[04:29] Jordan Kim: Full audit trail: who ran, when, input id, model version, and results. Logs are exportable and can be streamed to your SIEM.
[04:37] Priya Shah: What's the difference if we run this on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for us? Latency/cost differences aside, what about PHI compliance?
[04:48] Samir Patel: Hosted is fastest to get started, but for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives isolated capacity and tenant-level isolation; Private puts control of the control plane and network with you — can be VPC or on-prem. Both support KMS, RBAC, and audit retention controls.
[05:05] Marcus Lee: Good. For pilot we're open to Dedicated with restricted retention. What's the expected throughput for evals — we expect around 5k prompts/day during the benchmark.
[05:16] Lina Morales: That's small for us; batching helps. Eval jobs can be batched or streamed and we have cost profiling in Optimize to recommend batching and quantization for model variants.
[05:28] Priya Shah: We also want regression alerts to map to clinical severity levels — e.g., high severity if med list mismatch. Can severity be custom?
[05:36] Lina Morales: You can map tag-based rules to severity and then map severity to notification channels and SLA escalation policies.
[05:45] Dana Gomez: A concrete workflow: we run daily evals on a sample of production traffic, alerts go to a triage queue with examples, then SEs mark false positives to tune thresholds. Does Redwood support marking prompts as false positives and retriggering?
[05:58] Samir Patel: Yes — you can annotate prompts, mark them as FP/TN, and the system will retrain baseline thresholds or exclude them from future runs. There's also integration with your issue tracker for human review.
[06:12] Marcus Lee: How about A/B comparisons — do we get statistical tests baked in?
[06:17] Lina Morales: We provide a suite: bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation tests, and you can plug in your own analytics if you export raw scores.
[06:25] Priya Shah: Excellent. What about the API — can we programmatically kick off eval runs and pull metrics?
[06:31] Jordan Kim: Yes, full REST API and SDK support. You can POST a prompt set, poll job status, and GET aggregated metrics. We'll share SDK examples in Python and Go.
[06:41] Evan Brooks: Any rate limits? For the pilot we'll need bursts.
[06:46] Samir Patel: For Hosted we've got quota tiers, but for Dedicated we can provision burst capacity. We'll include recommended autoscale config for your expected load.
[06:56] Rafael Ortiz: Back to security—does Redwood store cleartext prompts by default?
[07:02] Avery Chen: By default we store encrypted at rest; for PHI customers we recommend encryption + tokenization or hashed storage. You can configure not to store the full prompt.
[07:12] Priya Shah: Can we run evals inside our VPC so data never leaves the network?
[07:17] Samir Patel: With Private deployment, yes, control plane can be customer-managed and inference/eval workloads can run in your VPC or on-prem.
[07:27] Marcus Lee: Let's talk about false positive rate on alerts — how do you recommend tuning?
[07:31] Lina Morales: Start with a conservative threshold, monitor precision/recall on labeled prompts, and use the evaluation UI to review top failing prompts. We also export confusion matrices.
[07:42] Dana Gomez: Any support for clinician-in-the-loop labeling?
[07:46] Lina Morales: Yes, you can add labels and feedback which flow back into your eval dataset and trigger re-eval.
[07:54] Priya Shah: Can we compare two models across different metrics and get a combined health score?
[07:59] Samir Patel: You can create composite scores by weighting metrics and visualize trade-offs in the A/B view.
[08:08] Marcus Lee: For the pilot, scope proposal? We want a 2-week benchmark with 5k prompts and daily evals, plus 1-week canary 10% traffic for live evals. Can Redwood run that?
[08:20] Avery Chen: Absolutely. Typical pilot: we run the offline benchmark first, then do a canary in production. We'll provide pricing for a Dedicated pilot and an SOW.
[08:30] Priya Shah: Any chance to do a technical deep dive on networking and deployment next week? Rafael and Evan should join.
[08:35] Samir Patel: Yes, we can do that. I'll prepare a VPC/private deployment architecture diagram and minimal firewall rules.
[08:43] (background typing)
[08:46] Rafael Ortiz: On incident response — if an eval catches a regression that's clinically severe, what's escalation?
[08:51] Jordan Kim: You can map severity to an escalation policy: immediate paging, Slack channel, and auto roll-back policies if you configure automated fallbacks.
[08:58] Priya Shah: How do automatic rollbacks work?
[09:01] Samir Patel: If you set a policy to fallback to a safe model variant on regression, the router will switch to the fallback model for the affected route until human intervention.
[09:10] Marcus Lee: Do we get token-level cost breakouts for running evals in Optimize?
[09:15] Lina Morales: Yes, Optimize shows per-token cost, recommended quantization, and batching to reduce cost while keeping SLOs.
[09:23] Evan Brooks: For our internal procurement we need ballpark pricing for a 2-week Dedicated pilot.
[09:27] Avery Chen: I'll follow up with pricing tiers and a pilot quote.
[09:31] Priya Shah: One more question — can Redwood detect data leakage between prompt sets? We had issues with test prompts appearing in training sets.
[09:40] Samir Patel: We have similarity-detection tools and fingerprinting to flag near-duplicates across uploads.
[09:47] Dana Gomez: Good.
[09:50] Lina Morales: Wrapping up, here's the checklist we usually follow for pilots: share eval template, provide sample prompts, configure retention/KMS, run offline benchmark, run canary, review alerts and tune thresholds.
[10:03] Priya Shah: Sounds good. Let's confirm dates — we aim to start first week of Dec.
[10:09] Avery Chen: We'll target pilot kickoff on 2026-12-07 pending legal and data prep.
[10:13] Marcus Lee: Legal will need the security pack and DPA.
[10:16] Rafael Ortiz: Also need evidence of SOC2 and penetration test history.
[10:21] Jordan Kim: We'll attach SOC2 and pen test summary in the security pack.
[10:25] Priya Shah: Great. Thanks everyone.
[10:28] Avery Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with next steps and share artifacts.

End of transcript.
